stemBlocks.value: Make x the subject of the formula y = (x - 4)/3.
Think first: The right-hand side subtracts 4 then divides by 3, so reverse both moves in the opposite order.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p056-q11 from workbook page 56.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply both sides by 3 to clear the fraction, then add 4.

whyThisWorks.value: Clearing the denominator first keeps the working free of fractions. Because the whole of x - 4 was divided by 3, the whole of it reappears when you multiply by 3 - that is why the answer is 3y + 4 and not 3y - 4 or 3(y + 4).

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying only the x by 3, giving 3y = 3x - 4.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Multiplying only the x by 3, giving 3y = 3x - 4.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding 4 before multiplying by 3, giving x = 3(y + 4).
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding 4 before multiplying by 3, giving x = 3(y + 4).

examTip.value: Clear fractions first: multiplying both sides by the denominator removes the most common source of slips.
